nodes.title: Simplifying fractions
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: To simplify a fraction divide both the numerator and the denominator by their greatest common divisor (GCD). A fraction is in its simplest form when the numerator and denominator share no common factor other than 1.

nodes.title: Comparing fractions
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: To compare two fractions rewrite them with a common denominator, then compare the numerators. Cross-multiplication is a shortcut: a/b versus c/d compares a*d to b*c.

nodes.title: Equivalent ratios
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: Two ratios are equivalent when they reduce to the same simplest form. Multiplying or dividing both parts of a ratio by the same non-zero number produces an equivalent ratio.

nodes.title: Solving linear equations
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: To solve a linear equation move all terms containing the variable to one side and all constants to the other, then divide by the coefficient of the variable. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other.

nodes.title: Quadratic equations
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: A quadratic equation is an equation that can be written in the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0, where a, b and c are constants and a is not 0. The highest power of the unknown is 2, so a quadratic equation has at most two solutions, called its roots. The three main ways to solve one are factorisation, completing the square, and the quadratic formula.

nodes.title: Solving quadratic equations by factorisation
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: To solve a quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 by factorisation, write it as a product of two brackets equal to zero, for example (x + p)(x + q) = 0. Find two numbers that multiply to give a*c and add to give b. Then use the zero-product rule: if (x + p)(x + q) = 0 then x + p = 0 or x + q = 0, giving x = -p or x = -q. For example, x^2 + 5x + 6 = 0 factors to (x + 2)(x + 3) = 0, so x = -2 or x = -3.

nodes.title: The quadratic formula
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: Any quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 can be solved with the quadratic formula x = (-b plus or minus the square root of (b^2 - 4ac)) divided by 2a. The expression b^2 - 4ac under the square root is called the discriminant: if it is positive there are two real roots, if it is zero there is one repeated root, and if it is negative there are no real roots. Use the formula when the equation does not factorise easily.

nodes.title: Laws of indices
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: Indices (powers) follow fixed laws. To multiply powers of the same base add the indices: a^m * a^n = a^(m+n). To divide, subtract the indices: a^m / a^n = a^(m-n). A power raised to a power multiplies the indices: (a^m)^n = a^(m*n). Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1: a^0 = 1. A negative index means a reciprocal: a^(-n) = 1 / a^n. A fractional index means a root: a^(1/n) is the nth root of a.

nodes.title: Mensuration: area and volume
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: Mensuration is the measurement of length, area and volume of shapes. Area of a rectangle = length * width; area of a triangle = 1/2 * base * height; area of a circle = pi * r^2. Volume of a cuboid = length * width * height; volume of a cylinder = pi * r^2 * h; volume of a cone = 1/3 * pi * r^2 * h. Always keep the units consistent and state area in square units and volume in cubic units.

nodes.title: Simultaneous linear equations
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: Simultaneous equations are two equations in two unknowns that are true at the same time. In the elimination method you add or subtract the equations to cancel one variable, solve for the remaining one, then substitute back. In the substitution method you make one variable the subject of one equation and substitute it into the other. Both methods give the same pair of values that satisfy both equations.

nodes.title: Percentages
nodes.subject: maths
nodes.body_markdown: A percentage is a fraction out of 100. To find a percentage of an amount, write the percentage as a fraction over 100 and multiply, for example 25% of 80 = 25/100 * 80 = 20. To write one quantity as a percentage of another, divide the first by the second and multiply by 100. Percentage increase or decrease = (change / original amount) * 100.
